translations.text: Christ was born at midwinter: the glory of kings, the famous prince, eternal and almighty. On the eighth day he was named Saviour, the guardian of the kingdom of heaven.

So at that same time the wide hosts, a countless people, hold the beginning of the year, because the calends, the first month, comes to our dwellings set on that same day. A great people long ago called it January.
And five nights after that, the baptism-time of the eternal Lord comes to us. The glorious, battle-brave men in Britain, here in this land, call it Twelfth Day.
Likewise, four weeks after that, less two nights, Solmonath comes to the dwellings: the coming of February, as wise companions, old men learned in the law, reckoned it long ago.
And one night after that we keep the mass of Mary, the King's mother, because on that day she brought Christ, the Ruler's child, to the temple.

Then five nights after that, winter is carried away from the dwellings. And after seventeen nights by count, the warrior, the Saviour's thane, famous Matthias, suffered death, as I have heard, after spring had come to the town, to men's dwellings.
Likewise it is widely known to peoples everywhere, to churls and earls, that three and two [nights] after that come its calends (except when a leap year is ordained in the fourth year;
then it comes one night later to our dwellings). Adorned with frost and with hail-showers, fierce March, lofty Hlyda, travels across the earth.
Then eleven nights after that, the holy and noble Gregory, famous in Britain, hastened into God's keeping.
Likewise, about nine nights after that, Benedict sought the Saviour, hardy and strong of mind. The wise praise him well in writings, the servants of the Ruler, men who keep the Rule.
Likewise, at that same time, those skilled in reckoning keep the equinox, because on that very day, at the beginning, the ruling God made the sun and the moon.
Lo, four nights after the equinox that men keep, the Father sent his archangel, who announced salvation to great Mary,
that she should bear the Lord, the best of kings, as it was made known throughout the world. That was a glorious event, renowned among the peoples!
Likewise, after four and three nights by count, the Saviour sends the month of April. In it the glorious time most often comes as a comfort to men: the Lord's resurrection.
Then joy is fitting, well and everywhere, as the prophet sang: "This is the day which the wise Lord made for us, for the generations of men, as a joy to all blessed dwellers on earth."

We cannot keep that time by a count of days, nor the Lord's ascension up into the heavens, because they always shift according to the decrees of the wise. Instead, one who is wise in years must find the holy days by skill in the cycle.
Yet we must still recount more commemorations of martyrs, set them forth in words and sing them wisely: that nineteen nights and five
after Eastermonath comes to us, people begin to raise up the relics, the holy treasures. That is a lofty day, a glorious time of prayer.
Likewise, six nights after that, beautiful Thrimilce comes gliding swiftly into the town, elegant in its trappings of woods and plants. May brings great benefit to the multitude everywhere.
So on that same day, noble companions, Philip and James, gave up their lives: brave young retainers, for the love of the Creator.
And two nights after that, God showed blessed Helen the noblest of trees, on which the Prince of angels, the Creator, suffered on the gallows for the love of men, by the Father's leave.
Likewise, after a week less one night, summer brings sun-bright days and warm weather to men's dwellings.

Then the fields quickly bloom with blossoms, and joy likewise rises across the earth among living creatures of many kinds. In many ways they speak praise to the King and glorify the famous one, the Almighty.

Eight and nine days after that, the Lord took Augustine into the other light, glad in his heart, because here in Britain he had found men humble toward God's will, as the wise Gregory had commanded him.

Never have I heard of any man, long ago or ever before, who brought better teaching over the salt sea, a more famous bishop. Now he rests in Britain, among the people of Kent, near the royal seat, in the glorious minster.

Then, after two and four [?] long, the month brings Earlier Litha to us in the dwellings, June into the land. In that month the gem rises highest into the heavens of all the year, the brightest of stars, and then descends from its height and sinks to its setting.
After that the fairest of lights, of all the world's creations, will look upon the ground longer and travel more slowly over the plain of the earth.
Then, after thirteen and ten nights besides, John, the thane of glory and the Lord's beloved, was born in days of old. We keep that feast at midsummer with great honour.
The feast of the saints Peter and Paul is honoured far and wide among the children of men, as is right and fitting.
Lo, the apostles, loyal to their Lord, suffered the cruel violence of the people at Rome, a glorious martyrdom, five nights after midsummer, as is well known;
The chief thanes had worked many wonders before throughout the nations, and after that they likewise performed countless clear and visible ones through the Son of the Creator.

Then soon, about two nights after that, July comes to us in due time. In that month, about twenty-four nights in, James gave up his life: strong in heart, wise and steadfast teacher of the peoples, the son of Zebedee.
And always about seven nights after that, Weed-month, brightened by summer, glides into the dwellings. Everywhere August brings Lammas Day to the peoples.
Then harvest comes after another such span, less one day, beautiful and laden with fruits. Wealth is shown fairly on the earth.
Then, three nights after that, the glorious deacon Lawrence, faithful to the Lord, departed through martyrdom. He now has life with the Father of glory as a reward for his works.

Likewise, five nights after that, the fairest of maidens, the glory of women, went to the God of hosts, because of her kinship with her Son, to a victorious home in paradise. The Saviour had then repaid the maiden with a fair reward for fostering him, eternal and forever.
Then always, ten nights after that, the feast of Bartholomew is honoured here in Britain, a very prosperous event.
Likewise, four nights after that, the death of the prince is made known widely to men: the warrior who once fittingly poured water over the royal Child of glory.
The Ruler said of him that no greater man was ever born of woman and man throughout the world.
And three nights after that, Holy-month (September), honoured by men, comes to the people among many nations, as the very wise [?]
the old wise men found long ago, the coming of September. And on the seventh day the best of women was born, the Lord's mother.
Then, after a number of days, thirteen, Matthew, the excellent thane wise in the gospel, sent forth his spirit to the Creator's decree, into eternal joy.
Then always, three nights after that, the day of the equinox comes far and wide to the nations, to the children of men.
Lo, in autumn we honour throughout the earth the feast of the archangel Michael, as many people know, five nights after the day of the equinox is shown to the peoples and to men.

And two nights after that, by wise counsel, the tenth month comes to the people: October, to our abundance in the dwellings. Winterfylleth is what the island-dwelling Angles and Saxons, men and women, call it far and wide.
Likewise, twenty and seven nights after that, they keep the feast of two warriors together on one day.
We learned long ago of those princes, Simon and Jude, that they were always very illustrious and dear to the Lord. Therefore they received glory, a blessed way up to heaven.

And four nights after that, the month quickly brings Blotmonath (Blood-month) into the dwellings, abundant for the people, food for men: November, which brings blessedness to the children of men and greater mercy from the Lord than any other month.
And on the same day we keep the feast of all the saints who, later or earlier, did the will of the Lord in the world.

Then, six nights after that, the day of winter goes forth far and wide. By the Lord's command it seizes the sun-bright autumn with an army of frost and snow, fettered with frost, so that the green fields, the ornaments of the earth, may not remain with us.
Four nights after that, the glorious Martin departed. The man without stain went to the Ruler, the guardian of the angels above.
Then twelve nights after that (eight and four), enemies of God sank the victorious man to the bottom of the sea, in the grey water. Many men have long called on him, Clement, often in their need.
And seven nights after that, noble Andrew, dear to the Lord of victory, gave up his spirit up into the heavens, into God's keeping, eager on the journey onward.
Then, on the next day, the month brings December into the dwellings for the people, for men, for the children of the nations: Earlier Yule.
Likewise, eight and twelve nights later by count, the Saviour himself gave bold-minded Thomas the eternal kingdom in return for his hardships, and gave his blessings to the brave warrior.
Then, four nights after that, the Father of angels sent his Son into this wide creation as a comfort to the peoples.
Now you can find the holy times that must be kept, as the command of the king of the Saxons extends at this same time throughout the kingdoms of Britain.
